final:
STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One stacked-call case reproduces a real gap: content added to an outer call's shadow root while an inner call is active is never hidden, and it stays visible after the inner call is cleaned up. Every other probe I ran passed, including nested targets, root handling, live announcers, shadow-host targets, and the flag-off path.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files created and deleted; `git status` matches the starting state: package.json, ariaHideOutside.ts, ariaHideOutside.test.js, yarn.lock).

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Stacked calls drop shadow-root observation while an inner call is active. The inner call's observer covers only its own `root` and its own shadow roots, and the outer observer is disconnected. Content added to the outer's shadow root during that window is never walked. After inner cleanup, the outer resumes observing, but the node added earlier is still visible. Criterion 4 (and 2 for the outer call) fails in this case. Repro: outer target is a button in shadow root S of host H (in body); inner target is a light-DOM span appended to H, so H stays visible to the inner call. Append an `<input>` to S while the inner call is active → `aria-hidden` is null. Call inner cleanup, append another `<input>` → `aria-hidden="true"`. Light-DOM stacking doesn't have this gap because the inner observer covers `body`. Suggested direction: keep the union of all live calls' shadow roots, or have the inner call also observe the enclosing shadow roots of the outer's targets.
- [minor] First attempt at the "target in shadow root is a direct child" check was my own probe error; the code correctly hid that sibling. Not a finding.
- [minor] `shouldUseInert` can't be exercised in jsdom (`inert` is unsupported, so `supportsInert` is false). Probing it there only verifies the aria-hidden fallback. Not a code defect.

CHECKS:
- Two-level nested target: siblings hidden at both levels, hosts on path not hidden, restored on cleanup → pass
- Target as direct child of shadow root, sibling in same root hidden → pass
- Additions deep inside non-target element in nested shadow root and direct to a shadow root → hidden; target-host shadow content untouched → pass
- Stacked outer + inner, addition during inner, then after inner cleanup → FAIL (during-inner addition not hidden) — blocking finding above
- Stacked control (outer only, addition to S) → hidden → pass
- `shouldUseInert` in shadow root: aria-hidden set, restored on cleanup, later additions not hidden → pass (fallback only)
- `root` = shadow host containing target: outer light siblings untouched, shadow siblings hidden, host not hidden, addition hidden → pass
- `root` inside a shadow root: siblings above root in same shadow root and host untouched → pass
- Same target passed twice, target that is a shadow host with its own content, additions into its shadow → pass
- `data-live-announcer` added directly to shadow root and top-layer element inside new container → stay visible → pass
- Flag off: shadow siblings of target not hidden, direct addition to shadow root not hidden, host not hidden → pass
- Triggered checks (invariants, nesting, new dependencies): the nesting checks are covered by the two-level and stacked probes above. I did not run a property-test loop over generated inputs or a `yarn install --immutable` check, so those are not checked.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Should the stacked-call gap above be fixed, or is it out of scope (the criteria mention only resuming on inner cleanup)? If it is in scope, the fix changes the observer model, so it needs a decision.
- Did you want a property-based loop (≥1000 generated trees) and a frozen-install run added to the check list? I did not run either.
